title: Evaluation of upper gastrointestinal tract surveillance in individuals with Lynch syndrome
summary: Patients with Lynch syndrome have an increased risk of Cancer in many different tissues. While screening for colorectal cancer by performing regular colonoscopies is well established in the various professional societies, this is not the case for cancer in the upper digestive tract (gastric or small bowel cancer). Thus, regular screening by gastroscopy is recommended in some countries but not in others. The EARLY study aims to compare these two strategies, i.e. regular screening by gastroscopy and not screening by gastroscopy.

interventions.name: Prospective observation of Lynch syndrome patients who receive endoscopic screening of the upper gastrointestinal tract by means of OGD (oesophagogastroduodenoscopy) based on national recommendations. Observation period 10 years (01.09.2024- 31.08.2034).

Prospective observation of Lynch syndrome patients who do not receive endoscopic screening of the upper gastrointestinal tract by means of OGD due to national recommendations.  Observation period 10 years (01.09.2024- 31.08.2034).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Signed informed consent
-      Patient must be able to follow study instructions and expected to attend and complete all required study visits. 
-	Confirmed diagnosis of a (likely-) pathogenic germline variant in MLH1, MHS2, MSH6, PMS2 or EPCAM (Lynch Syndrome)
Exclusion criteria:
-	Subjects without legal capacity who are unable to understand the nature, scope, significance and consequences of this clinical trial
-      Patients with a physical or mental condition that, in the judgment of the investigator, could pose a risk to the patient, confound the study results, or interfere with participation in the clinical study 
-      Personal history of duodenal or gastric surgery
